title: Thread dynamic HDR working directory through FFmpeg runner
summary: Threaded optional working-directory support through the shared native process runner and FFmpeg progress wrapper so future Dynamic HDR CPU/libx265 preservation can execute relative x265 artifact paths from a controlled base directory.
reason: Dynamic HDR x265 artifact paths are intentionally relative and colon-free. The FFmpeg runner needed explicit working-directory support and evidence before Do-Encode can safely inject extracted Dolby Vision RPU or HDR10+ JSON artifacts.
behavior_before: Invoke-NativeProcess and Invoke-FFmpegWithProgress always inherited the parent process working directory, and FFmpeg tool events did not record a working-directory base for relative artifact paths.
behavior_after: Invoke-NativeProcess, Invoke-NativeCommand, Invoke-ExternalToolCommand, Invoke-FFmpegCommand, and Invoke-FFmpegWithProgress accept an optional WorkingDirectory. The native runner resolves it before launch, records it on results, and FFmpeg started/completed events carry working_directory evidence.
tests_added: ops/pipeline/tests/Unit/Invoke-NativeProcessCleanupChecks.ps1 covers child process working-directory execution and result evidence.
ops/pipeline/tests/Unit/Invoke-FFmpegProgressChecks.ps1 covers FFmpeg wrapper working-directory propagation and event evidence.
rollback_plan: Revert this packet to remove the WorkingDirectory parameter plumbing, event fields, tests, generated summaries, and Dynamic HDR status wording; no source media or runtime state migration is involved.
